import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a visually appealing style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot to visualize the relationship between megapixels and price,
# differentiated by camera body type.
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='body_type',
    s=80,  # Adjust marker size for better visibility
    alpha=0.7, # Add transparency to handle overplotting
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Set y-axis to a logarithmic scale for better distribution visibility,
# especially if prices vary widely and are skewed towards lower values.
plt.yscale('log')

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Body Type (Log Scale Price)', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD, Log Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data points
plt.legend(title='Body Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0, frameon=True)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust plot layout to prevent labels/titles from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
